intro: Five problem-driven chapters. Each one opens on a failure that RAG teams describe in their own words, shows what QualityRag does about it with real SDK output, and ends on what it does not guarantee.
roadmap: It can't understand diagrams, images and video
Right rule, wrong customer or region
It works with one PDF, fails with more
The answer is in my documents, but RAG can't find it
We can't measure whether our RAG is improving
Excellent in the demo, unreliable in production
We can't guarantee who sees which documents
Too slow and expensive at scale
Vector search can't find exact product codes

chapters.title: It found the right document
chapters.complaint: “It found the right document, but gave the wrong answer.”
objectives: Remember
Name the three verdicts QualityRag can return: ADMIT, INCONCLUSIVE and REFUSE.
Understand
Explain why a set of relevant passages can still leave a requirement unsupported.
Apply
Run lab A1 and read which requirement each passage supports.
Analyze
Separate passages that are relevant from passages that are governing.
Evaluate
Judge whether an ADMIT result is enough to act on in a high-consequence workflow.
Create
Write a three-requirement PackSpec for a question from your own domain.

scenario.setup: Priya is the on-call lead for an EU payments team. At 02:10 the sanctions-screening dependency fails and the gateway stops. The team's assistant says on-call may restart it automatically.
dialogue: Junior
The assistant cited the handbook, an incident report and the runbook. Three citations. We're fine to restart, right?
Grumpy
Three citations about restarting in general. Not one about restarting the EU gateway when screening is down. Do you want to explain the fine to compliance?
Cloudina
Start from what the answer needs, not from what search returned. If the rule that governs this case never reached the model, the answer can't be trusted, however good the citations look.

concepts: Relevant is not sufficient
Retrieval ranks passages by similarity to the question. A passage can be on topic, recent and correctly cited, and still say nothing about the condition that decides the case.
Requirements first
A PackSpec lists what any answer to this kind of question must be backed by. QualityRag checks each requirement on its own and reports which ones have evidence.
Conditions need a reader
When a supporting passage contains words like unless or only, the console flags it. The passage still counts, but the check does not decide whether the exception applies. A person does.
chapters.hook: A requirement with no supporting evidence makes the whole result INCONCLUSIVE.

recall.q: When a requirement has no supporting evidence, the overall verdict is
The file that lists what an answer must be backed by is called a

chapters.lab_try: Remove the annex line from the second evaluation and run it again. Which requirement fails, and what reason does it give?

wargame.name: 02:10, gateway down
wargame.brief: The EU gateway is down. The assistant answered “yes, restart automatically” and cited four passages. Your compliance officer is asleep. Revenue impact is real, but so is a screening breach.

options: All four passages are about generic recovery. None covers the EU screening control.
Run the evidence check against the team's PackSpec
The check shows two of three requirements unsupported. You now know exactly what is missing.
Ask the assistant to double-check its answer
Asking again re-runs the same retrieval. It doesn't tell you what the answer needs.

steps.q: The check is INCONCLUSIVE: eu-screening-control and approval-or-exception are missing. Next?
options: Retrieve the EU controls annex and the regional memo, then check again
Targeted retrieval for the named gaps is the fastest route to a justified answer.
Override the check; the outage is costing money
An override skips the one rule that governs this case. That's the scenario the policy exists for.
Lower the requirement count to 1 overall
Changing the policy to fit the answer defeats the policy.

steps.q: Now the check ADMITs, and the annex says sign-off is required unless the emergency exception applies. Can you restart?
options: ADMIT means the declared checks passed. It is not authorisation to act.
Only after a person confirms whether the emergency exception applies, or gets sign-off
The condition is flagged for a human reader. Deciding it is your job, not the gate's.
ADMIT is enough to generate an answer. Acting on that answer still depends on the condition.

phases.title: Spot the gap
phases.task: A PackSpec has requirements recovery-procedure, eu-screening-control and approval-or-exception. Search returned two handbook passages for recovery-procedure and nothing else. What is the verdict?
hints: Count which requirements have any supporting evidence.
Two of three requirements have zero sources.
INCONCLUSIVE: insufficient independent evidence for two requirements.

phases.title: Name the reason
phases.task: Which reason does the SDK attach to the unsupported requirements?
hints: Nothing was too old, and nothing contradicted.
The count of independent origins is below the minimum.
INSUFFICIENT_INDEPENDENT_EVIDENCE.

phases.title: Read the boundary
phases.task: After targeted retrieval the verdict is ADMIT. Which statement is true?
options: The source documents are guaranteed to be true
The declared checks passed on the supplied evidence metadata
The exception has been verified to apply
hints: What does the gate actually inspect?
It inspects declared requirements and evidence metadata, not the world.
ADMIT means the declared checks passed on the supplied metadata.

quiz.q: Retrieval returned four relevant, recent passages. Can the answer still be unjustified?
options: Yes, if a governing requirement has no evidence
Only if the passages are older than a year
quiz.why: Relevance is about topic. Justification is about every requirement having evidence.

quiz.q: What does QualityRag check first?
options: Each requirement declared in the PackSpec
The similarity score of the top passage
quiz.why: Requirements are checked one by one, before any answer is generated.

quiz.q: An incident report says automated recovery reduced downtime. Which requirement does it support?
options: None; it is history, not authority
quiz.why: In the sample corpus the incident is linked to no requirement, so it isn't counted.

quiz.q: A supporting passage contains the word “unless”. What does the console do?
options: Counts it and flags the condition for a person
quiz.why: Qualifiers inside supporting spans are not evaluated by the gate. They are highlighted for a reader.

quiz.q: What should your application do on INCONCLUSIVE?
options: Withhold the answer and fetch the missing evidence
quiz.why: The verdict names the gap so you can retrieve for it.

deep.title: The rule in one line
deep.body: For each requirement r: let S(r) be the supporting evidence linked to r that is valid, fresh and not contradicted. r is admitted when |origins(S(r))| ≥ min_independent_sources(r). The result is ADMIT only if every r is admitted, REFUSE if any r has a contradiction, and INCONCLUSIVE otherwise. In lab A1 the first run has |origins| = 0 for two requirements, so the result is INCONCLUSIVE.

instructor.icebreaker: Ask each participant for one time an assistant gave them a confident answer that turned out to be missing a condition. Two minutes, no names of systems needed.
confusions: “ADMIT means the answer is correct.”
ADMIT means the declared checks passed on the supplied metadata. Show the README's decision semantics.
“The gate reads the passages.”
In v0.1 it reads evidence metadata (requirement links, origins, dates, status). Show the lab's ev() helper.
instructor.timing: Video 1.5 min · lab 10 min · war game 8 min · quiz 5 min. Skip the deep path if short on time.
instructor.activity: In pairs, write a three-requirement PackSpec for a question from your own work, then swap and try to find a passage set that would ADMIT a wrong answer.

chapters.title: When the evidence is missing
chapters.complaint: “It confidently invents an answer when the evidence is missing.”
objectives: Remember
State the three-way decision: generate on ADMIT, withhold on INCONCLUSIVE or REFUSE.
Understand
Explain why “not enough evidence” is a valid, useful answer.
Apply
Wrap a model call in answer_or_withhold() from lab A2.
Analyze
Trace how the gap list is built from the findings.
Evaluate
Assess the risk of calling a model without checking first.
Create
Design the message your users see when an answer is withheld.

scenario.setup: Marco runs customer support tooling at a travel company. A customer asks whether a fare rule applies after travel. The policy page that answers it was never indexed.
dialogue: Junior
The model still answered. It even gave a deadline. Isn't an answer better than nothing?
Grumpy
An invented deadline is worse than nothing. Someone in Canada found that out in front of a tribunal.
Cloudina
Give the application a third option: withhold. If the check can't admit the answer, say what's missing instead of guessing.

concepts: Abstention is a feature
Most pipelines have two outcomes: answer or error. QualityRag adds a governed third: the evidence is insufficient, and here is exactly which requirement is unsupported.
Check first, then generate
Call the evaluator before the model. Only an ADMIT result lets your code call the model with the admitted evidence.
The gap is the next action
The findings list each unsupported requirement by id. That list is what your application retrieves for next, or shows to the user.
chapters.hook: Only ADMIT lets your code call the model. Everything else withholds and names the gap.

recall.q: The one verdict that lets your code call the model is
In lab A2, the function that decides is called answer_or_____

case.name: Moffatt v. Air Canada
facts: Air Canada's website chatbot told a passenger he could claim a bereavement fare after travel, within 90 days.
The airline's policy page said bereavement fares could not be claimed retroactively.
Air Canada argued it was not liable for its chatbot's information. The tribunal held it liable for negligent misrepresentation.
Awarded C$650.88 in damages, plus C$36.14 pre-judgment interest and C$125 in tribunal fees.
case.lesson: A fluent answer is not evidence. An application that can withhold would have said the policy evidence was missing.

chapters.lab_try: Change answer_or_withhold() so the withheld message also prints the verdict reasons for each missing requirement.

wargame.name: The refund question
wargame.brief: Your support assistant is live. A customer asks whether they can claim a discounted fare after travelling. Retrieval returns a marketing page and an FAQ about booking, but not the fare-rules page.

steps.q: The check returns INCONCLUSIVE for fare-eligibility-rule. What should the customer see?
options: The model's best guess, with a small disclaimer
A disclaimer doesn't stop a customer relying on an invented rule.
A clear message that the rule couldn't be confirmed, plus a route to a person
Withholding with a reason and a next step is the governed outcome.
An error hides the reason. The gap is useful: name it.

steps.q: Your product manager wants fewer withheld answers. What's the right lever?
options: The SDK rejects a minimum below 1, and for good reason.
Index the fare-rules page and retrieve for named gaps
Fix the evidence supply, not the threshold.
Let the model answer when it is confident
Model confidence isn't evidence of anything the policy declares.

phases.title: Choose the gate
phases.task: Where should the evaluate() call sit?
options: After the model answers, to grade it
hints: What can you still prevent after the answer exists?
The point is to decide whether to generate at all.
Before the model is called.

phases.title: Build the gap
phases.task: Which findings go in the gap list?
options: Findings whose verdict is not ADMIT
Findings with more than one source
hints: You want what's missing.
Admitted requirements aren't gaps.
Findings whose verdict is not ADMIT.

phases.title: Know the limit
phases.task: Your code calls the model directly in one code path, without evaluate(). What does QualityRag do?
options: Nothing; enforcement is your application's job
Logs a warning to the model
hints: QualityRag is a library you call.
It can't see calls it isn't part of.
Nothing. Enforcement lives in your code.

quiz.q: Which result should withhold the answer?
quiz.why: Integrators should refuse or ask for more evidence on either.

quiz.q: What does INCONCLUSIVE give you that a generic error doesn't?
options: The ids of the unsupported requirements
quiz.why: The findings name each gap.

quiz.q: Does the base evaluator search again on its own?
options: No, re-retrieval is the application's job
quiz.why: The training guide says the base evaluator does not automatically search again.

quiz.q: In Moffatt v. Air Canada, what did the tribunal decide about the chatbot?
options: The airline was liable for what it said
The policy page excused the error
quiz.why: The tribunal rejected the separate-entity argument and found negligent misrepresentation.

quiz.q: Is a model call needed to evaluate the evidence?
options: No, the evaluator is deterministic and needs no model
quiz.why: No LLM is required for evaluation.

deep.title: Why abstention is cheap
deep.body: The evaluator is a pure function of the PackSpec, the evidence metadata and an as-of time. It makes no network or model calls, so you can run it on every request before generation. Its cost grows with the number of evidence rows, not with document size.

instructor.icebreaker: Show the Air Canada facts without the outcome and ask the room to predict the tribunal's decision.
confusions: “Withholding will annoy users.”
Compare an invented rule with a clear “we couldn't confirm this, here's a person”. Ask which one support would rather defend.
“QualityRag stops the model.”
It returns a verdict. Your code decides. Show the one-path-without-check boss phase.
instructor.timing: Video 1.5 min · case 5 min · lab 10 min · war game 6 min · quiz 5 min.
instructor.activity: Write the exact withheld-answer message for your product, including the gap and the next step. Read three aloud.

chapters.title: Are your sources independent?
chapters.complaint: “Three sources agree, but they all copied the same original.”
objectives: Remember
Recall that QualityRag counts distinct origins, not citations.
Understand
Explain why a mirror or a forwarded copy adds no corroboration.
Apply
Set min_independent_sources to 2 and run lab A3.
Analyze
Trace three citations back to their origin.
Evaluate
Decide when a requirement deserves two independent sources.
Create
Propose the origin metadata your ingestion should record.

scenario.setup: Lena reviews an internal research summary. It cites three sources that all agree. Two weeks later an auditor asks where each one came from.
dialogue: Junior
Three sources agree. That's strong corroboration, isn't it?
Grumpy
It's one handbook wearing three hats: a PDF, a wiki mirror and somebody's forwarded email.
Cloudina
Count origins, not citations. If your policy needs two independent sources, a copy can't be the second one.

concepts: The deceptive witness
Evidence that looks like support but isn't: a copy of the same original, an incident report treated as authority, a superseded runbook. Each adds a citation without adding independent support.
Origins decide independence
Every evidence row carries an origin. The evaluator counts the distinct origins among valid supporting rows and compares that number with min_independent_sources.
Metadata is the trust boundary
The origin is whatever your ingestion records. QualityRag counts it faithfully, but it doesn't yet verify authorship or catch a copy that hides where it came from.
chapters.hook: Three citations from one origin are one independent source.

recall.q: The PackSpec field that sets how many independent sources a requirement needs is min_independent_____

case.name: Mata v. Avianca, Inc.
case.court: U.S. District Court, S.D.N.Y. · No. 22-cv-1461 (PKC) · 22 June 2023
facts: Lawyers filed a brief citing judicial opinions that did not exist.
The opinions, with fake quotes and citations, had been generated by ChatGPT.
The court sanctioned the lawyers and their firm: US$5,000.
case.lesson: A citation that looks right is not support. Support has to trace back to a real, independent origin.
source: Reed Smith summary of Mata v. Avianca (S.D.N.Y. June 22, 2023)

chapters.lab_try: Give the forwarded email a different origin, “ops-team-inbox”. The verdict becomes ADMIT. Discuss: is that origin really independent? What would your ingestion need to know?

wargame.name: The audit trail
wargame.brief: An auditor is reviewing an answer that a policy admitted with min_independent_sources = 2. The evidence shows origins ops-handbook and ops-handbook-wiki.

options: Two origin labels were counted. Whether they're really independent depends on how they were assigned.
Whether the wiki is a copy of the handbook with a different origin label
Independence is only as good as the origin metadata.
Freshness matters, but it isn't the concern here.

steps.q: The wiki page is a copy. What's the fix?
options: Record origin from the source of truth at ingestion, so copies share it
Then the evaluator counts them once, as it does for the mirror in the sample data.
More copies with bad labels would still pass.
Copies will keep appearing. Fix the metadata, not the corpus.

phases.title: Count
phases.task: Rows: ops-7.3 (origin ops-handbook), ops-mirror-7.3 (ops-handbook), fwd-email-7.3 (ops-handbook). How many independent sources?
hints: Look at the origin column only.
All three share one value.

phases.title: Verdict
phases.task: The requirement needs 2. What's the verdict?
hints: Is anything contradicted?
No contradiction, but too few origins.
INCONCLUSIVE.

phases.title: Boundary
phases.task: Which of these can QualityRag v0.1 not do?
options: Count copies once when they share an origin
Verify who really authored a document
hints: Two of these are in the lab.
Authorship verification isn't in the evaluator.
Verify who really authored a document.

quiz.q: Three citations, one origin, min 2. Verdict?
quiz.why: One distinct origin is below the minimum.

quiz.q: What made lab A3 admit?
options: A fourth copy of the handbook
Minutes from the change board, a separate origin
quiz.why: Adding a genuinely separate origin raised the count to 2.

quiz.q: What was the problem in Mata v. Avianca?
options: Citations to opinions that did not exist
quiz.why: The cited opinions were fabricated by ChatGPT.

quiz.q: Where does the origin value come from?
quiz.why: The evaluator counts the origin it is given.

quiz.q: How does the console mark the mirrored handbook?
options: As the same origin, counted once
quiz.why: It shows “Same origin as ops-7.3: counted once, not twice.”

deep.title: Independence as a set
deep.body: independent_sources(r) = |{ e.origin : e ∈ valid supporting evidence for r }|. Duplicates collapse because a set has no repeats. The guarantee is therefore exactly as strong as the function that assigns origin. Two documents with different origin labels count twice even if one copied the other.

instructor.icebreaker: Hand out three printed “sources” that are visibly the same paragraph in different formats. Ask how many sources the group has.
confusions: “Different file formats mean different sources.”
Format is not origin. Show the mirror in the corpus: HTML, same origin.
“QualityRag detects plagiarism.”
It counts origin labels. Detection is upstream, in ingestion.
instructor.timing: Video 1.5 min · case 5 min · lab 10 min · war game 6 min · quiz 5 min.
instructor.activity: List the systems your documents come from and decide, for each, what its origin value should be.

chapters.title: Old rules and contradictions
chapters.complaint: “It uses outdated policies, and picks a side when documents disagree.”
objectives: Remember
Name the reasons STALE_EVIDENCE and CONTRADICTION.
Understand
Explain how max_age_seconds turns freshness into a requirement.
Apply
Run lab A4 with a one-year age limit.
Analyze
Explain why a contradiction produces REFUSE rather than INCONCLUSIVE.
Evaluate
Choose sensible age limits for different kinds of policy.
Create
Sketch how your ingestion would mark a passage as contradicting.

scenario.setup: Sam maintains runbooks for a platform team. A 2024 restart procedure still ranks first in search, and a newer memo says the EU approval rule supersedes it.
dialogue: Junior
The 2024 runbook is the top hit. Search thinks it's the best match.
Grumpy
It is the best match. It's also out of date. Similarity doesn't read the calendar.
Cloudina
Make freshness part of the contract, and make contradictions visible. Then the result can't quietly pick a side.

concepts: Freshness is declared
A requirement can set max_age_seconds. Evidence observed earlier than that is rejected with STALE_EVIDENCE before anything is counted.
Contradiction refuses
If any valid evidence for a requirement is marked CONTRADICTS, that requirement is REFUSE, and so is the whole result. The evaluator doesn't choose between documents.
The metadata knows the dates
The evaluator uses observed_at and status from your metadata. It doesn't read effective dates out of documents or spot supersession in free text. That is on the roadmap.
chapters.hook: Stale evidence is removed first. Any contradiction makes the result REFUSE.

recall.q: The PackSpec field that limits evidence age is max_age_____
A requirement with contradicting evidence gets the verdict

chapters.lab_try: Set max_age_seconds to three years and run again. Which reason disappears, and what happens to each verdict?

wargame.name: The superseded runbook
wargame.brief: Your assistant answered a restart question using the 2024 runbook. A memo from this year says the EU approval rule supersedes it.

steps.q: How should the restart requirement handle the 2024 runbook?
options: Set max_age_seconds so evidence older than the policy cycle is rejected
Freshness becomes part of the requirement, and the reason shows in the result.
Delete the runbook from the index
Deletion helps once. An age limit keeps working as documents age.
Trust ranking to prefer newer documents

steps.q: The current handbook supports a restart and the memo contradicts it. What should the result be?
options: ADMIT, because the handbook is newer
A contradiction is something a person resolves, with both sides visible.
INCONCLUSIVE means missing evidence. Here the evidence disagrees.

phases.title: Age
phases.task: max_age_seconds = 365 days. Evidence observed 2024-03-01, checked on 2026-11-05. What happens to it?
hints: How many days apart are the dates?
979 days is more than 365.
Rejected as STALE_EVIDENCE.

phases.title: Disagreement
phases.task: One fresh SUPPORTS row and one fresh CONTRADICTS row. Verdict?
hints: What does the evaluator do with CONTRADICTS?
Any contradiction sets the requirement to REFUSE.
REFUSE.

phases.title: Boundary
phases.task: Which can QualityRag v0.1 not do on its own?
options: Work out from raw text which document supersedes which
hints: Two of these were in the lab.
Supersession in free text needs extraction upstream.
Work out which document supersedes which.

quiz.q: What does STALE_EVIDENCE mean?
options: It was observed earlier than max_age_seconds allows
quiz.why: Age is computed from observed_at against the as-of time.

quiz.q: Why REFUSE rather than INCONCLUSIVE on a contradiction?
options: Evidence disagrees, which needs resolution, not more retrieval
quiz.why: INCONCLUSIVE means missing. REFUSE means contradicted.

quiz.q: In lab A4, the final result shows which reasons?
quiz.why: The stale runbook and the contradicting memo both appear.

quiz.q: Where does observed_at come from?
quiz.why: The evaluator only knows the dates you supply.

quiz.q: Evidence dated in the future is
quiz.why: The SDK rejects negative ages.

deep.title: Order of rejection
deep.body: Per evidence row the evaluator checks, in order: required fields present, a known status, a parseable date, not in the future, not older than max_age_seconds, then contradiction or support. So a stale contradicting row is rejected as stale before it can contradict. Lab A4's REFUSE comes from the fresh memo.

instructor.icebreaker: Ask who has followed a runbook that turned out to be superseded. What was the clue they missed?
confusions: “REFUSE means the answer is false.”
It means the declared evidence disagrees. A person resolves it.
“QualityRag knows document dates.”
It knows observed_at from metadata. Effective-date handling is a roadmap item.
instructor.timing: Video 1 min · lab 10 min · war game 6 min · quiz 5 min.
instructor.activity: For three of your policies, choose a max age and justify it in one sentence.

chapters.title: Broken tables
chapters.complaint: “My PDF tables are completely messed up. How would I even know?”
objectives: Remember
Recall that unverified extraction is UNKNOWN, not SUPPORTS.
Understand
Explain how flattening a table can move a condition.
Apply
Run lab A5 and compare the unverified and reviewed cell.
Analyze
Identify which of your sources have tables that matter.
Evaluate
Judge what “partial text only” coverage means for a result.
Create
Design a reviewer step that upgrades an extraction to SUPPORTS.

scenario.setup: Ade builds a fees assistant from PDF schedules. The parser flattens a table and the condition “waived above €10,000” lands next to the wrong number.
dialogue: Junior
The extracted text looks clean. The model read it fine.
Grumpy
Clean text that says the wrong thing. Every wire costs €25? Our biggest client will love that.
Cloudina
Treat an extraction nobody checked as unknown. Then it can't pass as evidence until someone compares it with the page.

concepts: Structure carries meaning
In a table, a value means something because of its row, column and header. Flattening to text can separate a value from its condition without any visible error.
Unknown is honest
An evidence row with status UNKNOWN is never counted as support. The result shows UNKNOWN_EVIDENCE, so the gap is visible.
Anchors, not answers

In the research track, Semantic Codex indexes CSV rows, PDF pages, DOCX paragraphs and subtitle times with a source anchor for every value, and marks coverage PARTIAL_TEXT_ONLY. It has no OCR yet, and table-structure validation is research.
chapters.hook: Unchecked extraction is UNKNOWN. It never counts as support.

recall.q: An extraction nobody has checked should have the status
Semantic Codex marks text-only coverage as PARTIAL_TEXT_____

chapters.lab_try: Add a second, reviewed cell for the same requirement from a different origin. Does the unverified cell still matter to the verdict?

wargame.name: The fee schedule
wargame.brief: Your fees assistant reads PDF schedules. A client is told every wire costs €25, but their transfers are above €10,000 and should be free.

steps.q: How should parsed table values enter QualityRag?
options: As SUPPORTS; the parser is reliable
That's how the wrong fee became evidence.
As UNKNOWN until reviewed against the page
Unknown never counts, so the answer is withheld until someone checks.
Then the fee question can never be answered.

steps.q: What should a reviewer record when a value is confirmed?
options: Change status to SUPPORTS, keeping the page and row anchor
The anchor lets anyone re-check the cell later.
Without the anchor nobody can audit it.
The verdict depends on the status you record.

phases.title: Status
phases.task: A cell read by the parser, not yet checked. Status?
hints: Has anyone confirmed it?
Unconfirmed is not support.
UNKNOWN.

phases.title: Verdict
phases.task: It's the only evidence for the requirement. Verdict and reason?
hints: UNKNOWN rows are not counted.
Zero sources, and the reason names the unknown row.
INCONCLUSIVE with UNKNOWN_EVIDENCE.

phases.title: Boundary
phases.task: What does QualityRag not do today?
options: Keep source anchors for indexed values
Repair or validate a broken table
hints: Two of these are in Semantic Codex v0.3.
Table repair is research.
Repair or validate a broken table.

quiz.q: Why is flattened table text risky?
options: Values can be separated from their conditions
quiz.why: Row and column structure carries meaning.

quiz.q: What does UNKNOWN evidence contribute to the source count?
quiz.why: Only SUPPORTS rows are counted.

quiz.q: What turned the lab's verdict into ADMIT?
options: A reviewer marking the cell SUPPORTS
quiz.why: The reviewed cell is valid support.

quiz.q: Does Semantic Codex v0.3 do OCR?
quiz.why: Its documentation says there is no OCR in this release.

quiz.q: Which is research, not shipped?
quiz.why: Checking table structure itself is still research.

deep.title: Anchors make review possible
deep.body: A source anchor (page 4, row 7, column 3) turns “check the extraction” into a bounded task: open one place and compare one value. Without an anchor, review means rereading the document. That's why anchors come before automated validation in the research plan.

instructor.icebreaker: Show a real fee or rate table and its copy-pasted text side by side. Ask what changed.
confusions: “A5 means QualityRag fixes tables.”
It doesn't. It stops unchecked values counting as evidence. Repair is research.
“Partial coverage means broken.”
It means stated limits: text only, no OCR, no images.
instructor.timing: Video 1.5 min · lab 8 min · war game 6 min · quiz 5 min.
instructor.activity: Pick one table your team relies on and write the review step that would upgrade its values to SUPPORTS.
